{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Graham John Hutchings''' is a British [[chemist]], Professor for Research at [[Cardiff University]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Prof Graham Hutchings - FLSW FRS |url=http://www.cardiff.ac.uk/chemy/contactsandpeople/academicstaff/hutchings-graham-overview_new.html |title=Professor Graham Hutchings BSc PhD DSc CEng CSci CChem FIChemE FRSC FLSW FRS |publisher=Cardiff.ac.uk |date=2011-05-27 |accessdate=2012-08-08}}</ref>

He gained his BSc in 1972 at [[University College London]], a PhD from University College in 1975 in Biological Chemistry and a DSc from the [[University of London]] in 2002 for his work on [[heterogeneous catalysis]].

His scientific career has included being Scientific Officer (1975–79) and Research and Production Manager (1979-1981) at [[ICI Petrochemicals]] and Chief Scientific Officer at AE & CI (African Explosives and Chemical Industries), Modderfontein, South Africa (1981–84). He was then in turn Lecturer, Senior Lecturer and Professor in the Department of Chemistry, [[University of the Witwatersrand]] (1984–87) followed by Assistant Director (1984–94) and Professor and Deputy Director (1994–97) at the Leverhulme Centre for Innovative Catalysis, [[University of Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.cardiff.ac.uk/chemy/contactsandpeople/academicstaff/hutchings-graham-biography_new.html|title= Prof Graham Hutchings - FLSW FRS|publisher= University of Cardiff|accessdate = 12 September 2013}}</ref>

He was then Professor of Physical Chemistry, [[Cardiff University]] (1997) and Head of School for Chemistry (1997–2006) and Professor of Physical Chemistry and Director of the Cardiff Catalysis Institute (2008-2019).<ref name = CSC>{{cite web|url = http://www.cardiff.ac.uk/chemy/newsandevents/news/royal-society-fellowship-award.html|title= Graham Hutchings elected FRS|publisher= Cardiff School for Chemistry|accessdate = 27 July 2013}}</ref>

From 2010 until 2013 he was chairman of SCORE, (Science Community Representing Education),<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=412478&sectioncode=26 |title=Appointments |publisher=Times Higher Education |date=2010-07-15 |accessdate=2012-08-08}}</ref> Director of the UK Catalysis Hub, 2012-2017 and 2018-2019, and President of the Faraday Division of the RSC 2012-2015. In 2016, Hutchings became the first Regius Professor of Chemistry of the University on the newly founded chair in Cardiff.<ref>{{cite web
 | url =https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-wales-south-east-wales-38264213
 | title =Cardiff University chemistry professor's royal title

==Honours and awards==
* 2009 Surfaces and Interfaces Award<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/archives/surfaces-and-interfaces-award/ | title=Surfaces and Interfaces Award }}</ref>
*2009 [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name = CSC/>
*2013 [[Davy Medal]] of Royal Society ''"for the discovery of catalysis by gold and for his seminal contributions to this new field of chemistry"'' <ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/awards/davy-medal/|title = Davy Medal - Most recent medallist|publisher = The Royal Society|accessdate = 12 September 2013}}</ref>
*2017 ENI Award for Advanced Environmental Solutions 
*2018 [[Faraday Lectureship Prize]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/FaradayLectureshipPrize/Index.asp|title=Faraday Lectureship Prize |publisher= RSC|accessdate= 19 May 2018}}</ref>
*2018  [[CBE]] in the [[2018 Birthday Honours|Queen's Birthday Honours]]<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2018/icheme-fellows-receive-queens-birthday-honours.aspx|title= IChemE Fellows receive Queen's Birthday Honours|publisher= IChemE|accessdate= 13 June 2018|archive-date= 13 June 2018|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180613210542/https://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2018/icheme-fellows-receive-queens-birthday-honours.aspx|url-status= dead}}</ref>
